{{Quote|Sir, the possibility of successfully navigating an asteroid field is approximately three thousand seven hundred and twenty to one.''"<br />"''Never tell me the odds!|C-3PO and Han Solo|audio=3720to1-TheOdds.flac|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The '''Hoth asteroid field''', also known as the '''Anoat Asteroid Belt''' and '''Hoth Asteroid Belt''', was an extensive, wildly erratic [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belt]] in the isolated [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth]] and [[Anoat system/Legends|Anoat systems]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Forged as the resulting effect of a collision between two rocky [[Planet/Legends|planets]] eons prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the belt was rich in untapped [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]] resources such as metal [[Ore/Legends|ore]], a magnet for [[Mining/Legends|mining]] prospectors hoping to make a fortune. However, it was plagued by [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based creatures like [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]] and the mighty [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorths]], or space slugs, which, coupled with ceaseless [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] collisions, imperiled any passing [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]]. The chaotic nature of the field further sent a constant bombardment of [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorites]] to the surface of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], the [[Star system/Legends|system's]] sixth planet.

The field was thus a favored sanctuary for those hoping to elude legal authority. Rampant criminal activity prompted [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement]], including [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]&mdash;such as [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], who once led a patrol for [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who apprehended a [[Alysun Celz|rogue Jedi]] on the [[Poison Moon]]&mdash;to investigate the field, though often unsuccessfully. Indeed, [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], most notoriously those of [[Clabburn the Elder]] in the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], proved an enduring presence in the Hoth asteroid field, which was populated by numerous bases from which raids were launched along the [[Anoat trade corridor]].

The elusive nature of the belt made the planet Hoth an ideal location for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion's]] [[Echo Base|headquarters]]. While the Rebels on Hoth monitored surrounding meteor activity for signs of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], their stay was short-lived. Spearheaded by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, the Empire forced the Rebels into retreat at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], scattering their forces. Consequently, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] braved the perils of the asteroid field in the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] as part of a desperate ploy to escape the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Starfleet]].

Believing the aspiring Jedi Rebel [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to be aboard the ''Falcon'', Vader deployed the full force of his [[Death Squadron|personal fleet]] and employed bounty hunters to track down the ship. For a while, it hid inside the asteroid field's [[Big One/Legends|largest planetoid]], where Solo and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] fell in love. After a close brush with [[Death/Legends|death]] in the belly of the gargantuan exogorth that made that asteroid its home and further Imperial pursuit, the crew of the ''Falcon'' successfully navigated the field's expanse against all odds.

Later, in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], [[Durga Besadii Tai|Durga the Hutt]] secretly constructed within the belt the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|Darksaber]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], designed to dominate [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. While the Jedi Luke Skywalker and [[Callista Ming]], having been rescued by Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo from the belt after their damaged ship was stranded there, failed to detect the Darksaber, it was soon discovered by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]]. A [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|Republic attack force]] under the [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] [[Battle for the Darksaber|pursued]] the [[Weapon/Legends|weapon]] through the field, ultimately destroying the Darksaber as it was crushed between two [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]].

==Description==
===Shards of two worlds===
{{Quote|Thank goodness, we're leaving the asteroid field!|C-3PO, aboard the ''Millennium Falcon''|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Arnod-DagobahLimited.png|thumb|right|300px|A cacophony of planetesimals surrounded the Hoth system.]]
The Hoth [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]], also named the Anoat Asteroid Belt<ref name="MTS">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> and Hoth Asteroid Belt,<ref name="Rebellion Era">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> was an especially wide swath of countless free-ranging planetesimals confined to erratic [[Orbit/Legends|orbits]] along the isolated [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system's]] ecliptic.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Occupying that system's outermost orbit but with stray bodies scattered throughout,<ref name="Databank" /> its reach extended to the nearby [[Anoat system/Legends|Anoat system]],<ref name="Bossk">{{StoryCite|story=The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> where it occupied the sixth orbit around the [[Anoat (star)|star of the same name]], between the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Deyer/Legends|Deyer]] and [[Pujool/Legends|Pujool]].<ref name="TEA" /> In close proximity to the [[Anoat trade corridor]] that connected the Anoat and [[Bespin system/Legends|Bespin systems]],<ref name="Illustrated" /> which were joined up with the Hoth system by the [[Ison Trade Corridor/Legends|Ison Corridor]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|space lane]],<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] field was situated in the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region<ref name="Javin" /> in the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]]<ref name="Region" /> and was the result of a collision billions of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Illustrated" />

The collision was between two large and rocky planets of the Hoth [[Star system/Legends|system]]. The worlds were fractured into scattered chunks of debris that were strewn throughout the system and eventually were pulled into erratic orbits around [[Hoth (star)/Legends|Hoth]], the system's [[Star/Legends|star]]. The largest asteroids, continually tugging at each other, destroyed any possibility of maintaining a rigid orbit.<ref name="Illustrated" /> The Hoth system's planets were the frequent recipients of [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorite]] collisions from asteroids that had broken away from the field as a result. In particular, a steady stream of meteorites constantly bombarded the [[Water/Legends|ice]] planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], occupying the system's sixth orbit as its outermost and sole habitable world.<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> Combined with the planet's three moons, large meteor impacts enacted tidal forces that cracked Hoth's ice shelves, allowing [[Geyser/Legends|geysers]] to erupt before the frigid [[Temperature/Legends|temperatures]] quickly sealed the breaches, forming darker and smoother ice. Meteor impacts also blasted smooth craters in the ice that made ideal ice-skating rinks.<ref name="Illustrated" />

[[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] and surveyors also speculated that the asteroid field may have formed after the crumbling of one of the planet Hoth's own [[Moon/Legends|moons]], or even that the two planets' collision caused the moons to crumble, supplementing the rock storm.<ref name="OSVC 13">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|13|In A Galaxy Far, Far Away}}</ref> The belt was also thought to potentially be the remains of an unformed planet.<ref name="FF67">{{FactFile|67|HOT 13-14|Hoth &ndash; Asteroid Belt}}</ref>

===Hazard zone===
{{Quote|<nowiki />''[H]''yperspace passage through the area ''[is]'' extremely difficult; even travel at sublight speeds is risky for all but the most skilled pilots.|Rebel Kem Monnon, commenting on Hoth's asteroid field|<ref name="Illustrated" />}}
[[File:Tieasteroid.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A TIE Fighter collides in the maelstrom.]]
Throughout the belt's existence, rocky chunks continued to constantly collide with one another, grinding each other down to smaller asteroids.<ref name="Illustrated" /> During the belt's early years, the collisions were catastrophic, creating vast craters in the many large asteroids. The collisions became less frequent and less powerful by comparison as the field matured, and the asteroids entered relatively stable orbits.<ref name="FF67" /> As the asteroids collided and increased in number, the composition<ref name="Illustrated" /> of the belt's thickest region<ref name="Databank" /> grew in range from microscopic dust particles to tiny pebbles, large boulders, and,<ref name="Illustrated" /> in the Anoat system,<ref name="FF67" /> irregularly shaped [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]]<ref name="Illustrated" /> that rivaled small moons in size.<ref name="FF67" />

The Hoth asteroid field threatened to pulverise any spacecraft that chanced its<ref name="ESB" /> random maelstrom and constant collisions;<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> it was a certain [[Death/Legends|deathtrap]] for [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] hoping to successfully traverse the field. The chaotic nature of the asteroid field thus created an environment all but impossible for charting, proving a great hazard for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel through the remote region.<ref name="Illustrated" />

Dotted with craters and narrow gorges, larger asteroids also featured fissures and spacious [[Cave/Legends|caves]]; giant [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorths]] dwelled within them and consumed surrounding rock as part of its [[Diet/Legends|diet]], enlargening its burrows in the process.<ref name="FF67" /> Some asteroids were massive enough to contain scant [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]]<ref name="Illustrated" />&mdash;when the [[Human/Legends|Humans]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] inadvertently explored the belly of an exogorth living inside an asteroid, they simply wore [[Roamer-6 breath mask/Legends|Roamer-6 breath masks]].<ref name="ESB" />

===Geology and fauna===
{{Quote|Aaagh! Go away, go away, beastly thing! Shoo! Shoo!|C-3PO cries futilely at mynocks, who are probing the ''Millennium Falcon''|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Hothslug.jpg|thumb|right|320px|A 900-meter-long exogorth emerges from one of the field's largest asteroids.]]
The field's asteroids were rich in [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]] composition, the lasting deposits of the two planetary cores.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Indeed, the asteroids were composed of a vast array of different minerals and metal [[Ore/Legends|ores]],<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> including [[nickel]]<ref name="Payback">{{StoryCite|story=Payback: The Tale of Dengar|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> and [[Iron/Legends|iron]]<ref name="Boba">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>&mdash;one asteroid was even rumored to be comprised entirely of [[Platinum/Legends|platinum]].<ref name="Illustrated" /> The high metal concentration of the asteroids had a tendency to cause [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] distortions for passing [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="Payback" />

A rare growth found among many of the asteroids were [[crystal fern]]s, strange transparent, [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] produced as an effect of some rocks' exposure to heavy [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]] and cold [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]]. The crystals grew in delicate, web-like tangles extending several [[Meter/Legends|meters]] from their base on the surface of an asteroid and propagated from one asteroid to another, broken in shards that were carried to other rocks by orbital forces.<ref name="Illustrated" />

The asteroid field's very high mineral content and presence of some organic material, including frozen water, meant that some extraordinary creatures occupied the asteroid field.<ref name="OSVC 13" /> Many of the larger asteroids were inhabited by the [[Worm/Legends|wormlike]] exogorths, colloquially called "space slugs"<ref name="Rough" />&mdash;one of the largest creatures known to the [[Universe/Legends|universe]]. Those inhabiting the Hoth asteroid field were the largest recorded. Aside from silicon, exogorths also consumed organics by ingesting passing starships and other creatures,<ref name="FF67" /> posing a severe threat to space travel and mining in the belt.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Prior to the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="Rough" /> the [[Realspace/Legends|space]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Clabburn the Elder]] installed the space [[Slug (creature)/Legends|slugs]] as guardians within the hollow shaft entrances of asteroids that led to his secret hives of operation.<ref name="Illustrated" />

In low asteroidal [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]<ref name="Illustrated" /> and over many [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]],<ref name="FF67" /> these space slugs grew to enormous proportions, some reaching lengths of 900 meters. The slugs were able to survive within the thin atmospheres of the larger asteroids, subsisting for many years by breaking down the rock of the asteroid itself. Long tendrils extended from the rear portion of the creatures that reached into the asteroids to extract nutrients.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Slugs in old age would petrify, transforming into caves themselves.<ref name="Enviorama">{{SideshowCite|set=Polystone Dioramas|pack='This Is No Cave' (Space Slug Enviorama)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/SSCDIOspaceslug.asp}}</ref >By the early years of the Galactic Civil War, thousands of space slugs populated the asteroid field.<ref name="Rough" />

In turn, winged, parasitic creatures known as [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]] inhabited these giant space slugs. Silicon-based lifeforms able to survive in vacuum,<ref name="Mynock Databank">{{DB|creature|mynock|mynock}}</ref> mynocks typically assumed sanctuary within their hosts and leached off the soft inner membranes of the slugs' interiors and the thermal energy they radiated as heat. Large numbers of mynock packs lived in the field, attaching themselves to the outer hull of the occasional passing starship to drain the vessel's concentrated energy.<ref name="Illustrated" />

==History==
===Smugglers' cove===
[[File:Hoth_Asteroid_Belt_TESB.png|thumb|left|300px|Hidden in the asteroids were valuable mineral deposits.]]
The asteroid belt was an opulent source of untapped wealth for [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large. The mineral deposits laying in store within the asteroids themselves promised instant reward to anyone who was able to extract them. For many years prior to the fall of the Galactic Republic, Hoth's asteroid belt was a powerful attractant to several such prospectors&mdash;independent, or otherwise&mdash;hoping to strike it rich. The belt's hazardous and erratic pitfalls were not enough to deter these entrepreneurs from accepting the gambit of potential death for wealth.<ref name="Javin" /> Nevertheless, by [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]],<ref name="Darksaber date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']] to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]].</ref> the field's resources still remained largely untapped despite previous efforts.<ref name="Darksaber" />

A popularly persistent legend existed of one particular asteroid that was rumored to be nothing less than a mass of nearly pure platinum. The chunk of ore became anecdotally known as [[Kerane's Folly/Legends|Kerane's Folly]] because the prospector [[Kerane]], having supposedly discovered the asteroid, extracted a sample and exited the asteroid field in order to confirm that it was indeed the precious metal he sought. When he returned to the field, he found he could not relocate his treasure. Kerane spent the rest of his life searching the Hoth asteroid field, but was never able to recover the asteroid. This story had spurred other prospectors into searching for the platinum asteroid for years without success.<ref name="Illustrated" />

[[File:Hothasteroidfieldpoisonmoon.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The Poison Moon asteroid]]
For centuries the field also proved to be a favorite hiding place for many [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and pirates.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Rumors abounded about pirate treasure that lay hidden deep within the field.<ref name="Javin" /> The larger asteroids with minimal atmospheres served as strongholds for many hostile criminals, where they discovered they were relatively safe from any lawful hand of judgment. Governmental organizations alike, from the Republic and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], to independent planetary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police forces]], had lost elusive prey into the confines of the wild asteroid assortment. They each determined that, after numerous enforcement ships were lost in pursuit, once a refugee managed to reach the asteroid belt, continuing the chase was an exercise in futility.<ref name="Illustrated" />

Reports of smugglers raiding a small [[Mining/Legends|mining]] [[Space station/Legends|station]] in the asteroid field came to the attention of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] sometime prior to<ref name="Power">''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]''</ref> the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The responsibility fell to [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] to assemble a team of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to patrol the area for suspicious smugglers.<ref name="Power" />

===Distress on Poison Moon===
{{Quote|Isn't it ''funny'' how appearances can be deceiving, ''little Padawan''?|Alysun Celz speaks to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Poison" />}}
[[File:Mynock_attack.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Mynocks attack the Dark Jedi Alysun Celz.]]
One large asteroid in particular was known among pirate groups as the [[Poison Moon/Legends|Poison Moon]] because of its surface appearance.<ref name="Poison" /> In [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]]&mdash;three years prior to the onset of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="Poison date">The events of "[[Poison Moon (comic story)|Poison Moon]]" take place three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which was in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. The events of ''Poison Moon'' must therefore take place in [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]].</ref>&mdash;the Republic [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]] ''[[Radiant IX]]'' was sucked into the [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]] of the asteroid after a group of mynocks leeched power from the exterior of the ship. The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] learner, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], arrived at the crash site responding to a [[Distress beacon/Legends|distress beacon]]. They discovered the ''Radiant IX'' had been carrying a group of Jedi en route back to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where they hoped to deliver the captive [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Alysun Celz]] to the Jedi Council. Kenobi and Skywalker were able to rescue the lone Jedi survivor, [[Et Rex]], and detain Celz.<ref name="Poison" />

===Pirates galore===
{{Quote|I have managed to come upon one in an asteroid field outside the Hoth system&hellip;The creature is 900 meters long. To extricate it from its present lair, we'll need to hire a Corellian towing ship and two Bith industrial power winches. We'll also need a tank of sedative to knock the creature unconscious. In addition, you'll need to lace your asteroids with katrium on a regular basis, which will make the space slug sterile and lock it at its present size. You don't want this one to get any larger.|Gamgalon responds to an advertisement calling for a healthy exogorth|<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>}}
Sometime prior to the fall of the Republic,<ref name="Rough" /> the [[Mugaari]] pirate [[Icanis Tsur]] and a crew of thirty manning his ship, the ''[[80-Vag]]'', were killed when the craft was destroyed within the field. The ship's wreckage was pilfered by [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] teams and rogue [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] as it floated among the asteroids. However, many of these foragers were similarly destroyed in the process, adding to the very debris they were hoping to retrieve.<ref name="Javin" />

[[File:The_Jewel_of_Yavin_Coverart_by_Mark_Molnar.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Hoth asteroid field neighbored the resorts of Bespin.]]
The asteroid field was also known notoriously as the haven of operations for the pirate Clabburn the Elder, an uncompassionate Mugaari, during the last decades of the Republic.<ref name="Rough" /> Striking from the safety of the field, Clabburn and his forces would stalk the most populated hyperlanes running through the Anoat trade corridor, typically attacking wealthy tourists in [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liners]] en route to the nearby resort of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in the Bespin system.<ref name="Illustrated" />

[[Bounty hunter/Legends|Bounty hunters]], police forces, and vengeful family members of the besieged attempted to hunt Clabburn, but were unable to locate his base within the field. The pirate took precaution to constantly relocate from one planetoid to another, always covering his tracks and booby-trapping his previously used facilities. Clabburn acquired and installed giant exogorths at the entrances of his discarded bases to devour anyone brave enough to track him.<ref name="Illustrated" /> [[Spacer/Legends|Spacer]] legend later recounted Clabburn's use of space slug guardbeasts for his mobile asteroid headquarters, while other legends mentioned that those slugs grew to ginormous proportions due to the field's lack of gravity.<ref name="Databank" />

At some point following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], another Mugaari pirate, [[Clabburn the Younger]], the son of the elder Clabburn, attempted to fashion his own pirating career after that of his father. He similarly created a secret base within the field, drilled deep into the nickel-iron core of one of the larger asteroids, known as [[Airtight Base/Legends|Airtight Base]] for its impregnable security. Also like his father before him, the younger Clabburn used some of the field's exogorths, which had multiplied to thousands in number by this [[Time/Legends|time]], as a security measure. He planted them in caves flanking Airtight Base, training them to attack a threatening ship by way of ultrasonic signal.<ref name="Rough" />

[[File:Gamgalon.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Gamgalon eyed the hunting of exogorths.]]
Sometime after Clabburn the Elder introduced the slugs to the field, the [[Krish (species)/Legends|Krish]] game [[Hunting/Legends|hunter]] [[Gamgalon]] responded to an advertisement placed on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] calling for a healthy space slug, declaring that he had discovered a 900-meter-long specimen in the Hoth asteroid field and that he believed he could deliver it in a couple [[Standard week/Legends|weeks']] time. However, he noted the difficulty in capturing the slug, explaining that he would require a special towing ship and heavy extraction machinery, a substantial amount of sedative to incapacitate the slug, and would potentially demand more than the originally advertised 100,000-[[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]], depending on the difficulty of securing the creature from its Hoth asteroid field home.<ref name="EGAS" />

===Some strike it Hoth===
====Rebel activity====
{{Quote|There's a meteorite that hit the ground near here. I want to check it out. It won't take long.|Luke Skywalker, believing to have sighted a meteorite from the field impacting the planet Hoth|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Wyron_serper.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Captain Serper at work at Echo Base]]
In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic's]] [[Alliance High Command/Legends|High Command]] established the secret [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the planet Hoth.<ref name="ESB" /> As observed by the base's leading engineer, [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Kem Monnon/Legends|Kem Monnon]]&mdash;who compiled a report on Hoth and the asteroid field's effects there<ref name="Illustrated" />&mdash;the world's remote nature and perpetual bombardment of meteorites proved to be a perfect natural camouflage from the probing eye of the Empire.<ref name="FF67" /> Nevertheless, the system's constant meteor activity was a hindrance to any attempts to track would-be approaching ships.<ref name="ESB" /> In response, the Alliance established [[Echo Station/Legends|Echo Stations]] around the planet Hoth to monitor the Hoth system's meteor activity and detect signs of Imperials;<ref name="Illustrated" /> the task fell to Echo Base scanner [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Wyron Serper/Legends|Wyron Serper]] to determine what was an asteroid and what could be an Imperial [[Scout ship/Legends|scout ship]].<ref name="Insider 74">{{InsiderCite|74|Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth}}</ref>

{{RPGseed}}
As Echo Base neared completion that year,<ref name="Date">''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]'' states that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] is "nearing completion, but is already in partial operation" and that "[[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] has recently settled into the facility." ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma's]] decision to establish the Rebel command headquarters on Hoth and Echo Base's completion to [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], thereby establishing the [[Time/Legends|time]] frame for ''Strongholds of Resistance''.</ref> a group of Rebels were assigned to deliver a supply shipment&mdash;including construction equipment, [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]], [[Droid/Legends|droids]], and other items&mdash;to the Rebel facility on Hoth. Upon arriving in the Hoth system, the Rebel [[Courier/Legends|couriers]] found themselves somewhat off course and had to traverse a section of the Hoth asteroid field before landing on the ice planet.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance">''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]''</ref>
{{Endgame}}

When an Imperial-launched [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] crashed into the planet Hoth<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Rebels failed to detect it as a threat. Jedi-aspirant&ndash;cum&ndash;Rebel [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], unfazed by yet another meteorite impact, reasoned it could have been a man-made instrument. Distracted by the crash, Skywalker was assailed by a [[Unidentified wampa/Legends|native wampa beast]] and nearly killed. The Rebels investigated the "meteorite" later on, only to realize that it was indeed an Imperial [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]]. The Alliance began evacuating Echo Base, as the droid had informed the Empire of their presence, leading to the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].<ref name="ESB novel" />

====Running the blockade====
{{Quote|What are you doing? You're not actually going into an asteroid field?''"<br />"''They'd be crazy to follow us, wouldn't they?|Princess Leia Organa and Han Solo|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Falconchase-CHRON.jpg|thumb|left|260px|TIE Fighters pursue the ''Millennium Falcon'' across one of the larger asteroids.]]
Instead of maintaining a distance from the Rebel sensors and obscuring itself under the asteroid field's chaos, the Imperial fleet, under [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel's]] [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]], exited hyperspace close to the Hoth system. The Imperial enforcer [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader deemed the move foolish and executed Ozzel, but the Empire still successfully invaded Echo Base. As they did so,<ref name="ESB" /> many fleeing Rebel ships were able to use the asteroids to their advantage to evade the Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the planet<ref name="FF67" /> and enter hyperspace. Among the last Rebels fleeing Hoth were Solo and his smuggler partner, Chewbacca, aboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] with [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Leia Organa and the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] in tow. They were followed closely by Vader's personal [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]].<ref name="ESB" />

Much to the chagrin of Solo and his passengers, the ''Falcon''{{'s}} malfunctioning [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] failed to engage, trapping them in realspace. While Solo feverishly worked on the ship's interior systems in an attempt to effect their escape from the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Starfleet]], Organa inadvertently piloted the ''Falcon'' into the Hoth system's asteroid field. Stuck&mdash;quite literally&mdash;between a rock and a hard place, Solo had little alternative but to plunge his ship further into the asteroids. Through masterful flying and near-suicidal maneuvering,<ref name="ESB" /> he escaped from a [[Flight group/Legends|flight]] of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]], led by [[Arnod (Galactic Empire)|Arnod]],<ref name="GG5">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> whose [[TIE pilot|pilots]] were unable to avoid crashing into the asteroid maelstrom. Solo eventually piloted his ship into a cavernous opening of [[Big One/Legends|one of the biggest asteroids]],<ref name="ESB" /> located in the Anoat system's portion of the field,<ref name="FF67" /> where he hoped to hide long enough to complete repairs on his hyperdrive.<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:Outrider-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Dash Rendar's ''Outrider'']]
Almost simultaneously, the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]], who had also escaped from Hoth after delivering a shipment of supplies to Echo Base, was similarly chased into the asteroid field by an [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] and a large contingent of its [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] complement. Unlike Solo, Rendar's ship, a sleek [[YT-2400 light freighter/Legends|YT-2400 light freighter]] named the [[Outrider/Legends|''Outrider'']], was not in disrepair. Rendar manned his [[Freighter/Legends|freighter's]] heavy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] while his copilot droid, [[LE-BO2D9/Legends|LE-BO2D9]], flew the vessel into the field after bypassing the Star Destroyer, which remained at the fringe of the belt. Rendar was able to hold off several [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] of TIE Fighters and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bombers]] long enough until the ''Outrider'' was far enough away from the asteroids to safely make the jump into hyperspace.<ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref>

One of Echo Base's thirty [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]] that attempted to escape through the Imperial blockade of the planet, the ''[[Treasure Trove]]'', was crippled and lost within the asteroid belt during the battle. The [[Transport/Legends|transport]] managed to dock along the edge of a crater on a large asteroid the size of a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]. Rebel [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] noticed the transport missing when it failed to regroup with the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] at the Rebels' predetermined [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] beyond the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|Galactic Rim]], where it was meant to deliver a valuable shipment of [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]]. He dispatched a team of special agents aboard the ''[[Out Runner]]'', a [[YL-2200 light freighter]], who located the ''Treasure Trove'' in the field, only to find its crew dead.<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>

Once the Rebel agents returned to the ''Out Runner'', they were beset upon by the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter [[Chreeto]] the Defiant and his crew, operating as Imperial retainers. Hoping to capture the Rebels, Chreeto pursued the ''Out Runner'' through the asteroid field in his [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]], the ''[[Prowling Wolf]]''. The Rebels, however, successfully escaped the bounty hunters.<ref name="GG3" />

At one point, a [[Unidentified Rebel pilot (Anoat system)|Rebel pilot]] captured by the Empire and scheduled for interrogation aboard a [[Imperial officer/Legends|naval officer's]] first command was rescued by the [[Medic/Legends|medic]] [[Ahleazah]], and together they fled via [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] just as the Imperial ship entered hyperspace near the Anoat system. The main Imperial task force then headed into Anoat's asteroid field, allowing a Rebel search and rescue team to retrieve the escape pod.<ref name="Herrogues">''[[Heroes & Rogues]]''</ref>

===Search for the ''Millennium Falcon''===
====Advancing the ''Avenger''====
{{Quote|Our ships have sighted the ''Millennium Falcon'', Lord, but it has entered an asteroid field, and we cannot risk&mdash;''"<br />"''Asteroids do not concern me, Admiral. I want that ship, not excuses.|Admiral Firmus Piett and Darth Vader|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:ThisCantEndWell-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Death Squadron strode into the asteroid field, pursuing the ''Falcon''&hellip;]]
Despite the threat of damaging asteroid collisions, the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] boldly led Death Squadron's chase of the ''Millennium Falcon'' into the field. Once the ''Millennium Falcon'' disappeared from sight, however, the ''Avenger'' slowed its pursuit near the edge of the belt. Vader nevertheless ordered his fleet of Star Destroyers into the asteroid onslaught. He believed that Luke Skywalker had escaped Hoth aboard the ''Millennium Falcon'' with the rest of his companions.<ref name="ESB novel" /> All of Vader's Star Destroyers, including his own [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the 19-[[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-long [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], were diverted into the asteroid field amid a flurry of damaging collisions and incidental casualties suffered aboard several of the Star Destroyers.<ref name="Anakin Skywalker: The Story of Darth Vader">''[[Anakin Skywalker: The Story of Darth Vader]]''</ref> [[Unidentified Imperial-class Star Destroyer (asteroid collision)|One]] Star Destroyer was obliterated by a single asteroid strike at its [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] tower.<ref name="ESB" />

Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]], commander of the ''Avenger'' at the forefront of the fleet, reasoned with Vader that the ''Millennium Falcon'' must have been destroyed, but Vader knew better. He ordered the ''Executor''{{'s}} Admiral [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] to dedicate every ship of Death Squadron to the search effort. The ''Avenger'' continued to charge forward, clearing a path through the asteroids for the remainder of the fleet to follow, while flights of TIE [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] littered the biggest asteroids with explosives, hoping to chase out their quarry. At Vader's request, the ''Executor'' alone exited the asteroid field for a while to facilitate a clear [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] transmission between him and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]&mdash;he instructed Vader to capture or destroy Luke Skywalker lest the Rebel was to become a Jedi.<ref name="ESB" />

====A rocky romance====
{{Quote|You can't make the jump to lightspeed in this asteroid field!''"<br />"''Sit down, sweetheart. We're taking off!|Leia Organa and Han Solo, as the ''Falcon'' flies out of the exogorth|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:YouCanProbablyBuffThatOut-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|right|300px|&hellip;though the Star Destroyers fell victim to tumbling asteroids.]]
The ''Millennium Falcon'' spent several days hiding within the massive asteroid while Solo and his passengers worked to repair the ship's faulty hyperdrive.<ref name="GG3" /> Solo shut down the ship's primary systems in order to avoid detection by the probing Imperial ships the group could hear overhead trying to chase them out. It was while cooped up within the close confines of the ''Millennium Falcon'' that the longstanding romantic tensions between Solo and Organa began to blossom. The princess finally warmed to Solo's roguish charms as they shared one of their first kisses within the deep innards of the asteroid.<ref name="ESB" />

However, it was not the might of the Imperial Starfleet that eventually flushed the ''Millennium Falcon'' out of its hiding place. The group soon discovered that mynocks living inside of the cavern had attached themselves to the ship's power cables, leeching the ship of its energy. While clearing the ship of the parasites, Solo and Chewbacca unwittingly discovered the true nature of their hiding spot. Stray [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts fired into the walls of the cave had caused the grotto to shake violently. It was not a simple cave that Solo had hidden his ship in, but the nesting area of a giant exogorth.<ref name="OSVC 13" />

====High-speed turnaround====
{{Quote|They can't have disappeared. No ship that small has a cloaking device.''"<br />"''Well, there's no trace of them, sir.|Captain Needa and [[Nemet/Legends|another officer]] aboard the ''Avenger'', having just lost track of the ''Millennium Falcon''|audio=Needa-Nemet.flac|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:PunyFalconRunsAway-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Star Destroyer ''Avenger'' chases the ''Millennium Falcon'' out of the asteroid field.]]
Solo was able to pilot his ship out of the closing jaws of the massive space slug with only [[Standard second|seconds]] to spare. As the Rebels expected, they were once again engaged by the Imperial fleet upon reentering the asteroids: Two TIE scout ships detected the ''Millennium Falcon'' and broke orbit, returning to the main Imperial fleet.<ref name="C-3PO: Tales of the Golden Droid">''[[C-3PO: Tales of the Golden Droid]]''</ref> Alerted, the ''Avenger'' soon continued chasing the ''Falcon''. Fortunately for the Rebels, they exited the confines of the asteroid field after traversing its expanse. Free of obstruction, Solo once again tried to engage his hyperdrive with repairs believed completed, only to find, much to the dismay of everyone aboard, it was still inoperable.<ref name="ESB" />

The ''Avenger'' was the only ship attached to Death Squadron that managed to stay with the ''Falcon'' through the entirety of the asteroid field, earning the [[Warship/Legends|warship]] a reputation for persistence among the Imperial Starfleet. Needa had sent his Star Destroyer headfirst into the asteroids as Vader had commanded, sustaining substantial damage in the process. It was all his [[Gunner/Legends|gunnery]] crews could do to try and keep up with the endless task of trying to shoot down the rocky debris in the Star Destroyer's path. So, when Solo suddenly and unexpectedly banked the ''Millennium Falcon'' on an attack course straight for the pursuing ''Avenger'', Needa and his crew were ill-prepared and lost the Rebel ship for good. Vader subsequently executed Needa for his failure.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:WhoWillTicketVaderForLittering-ESB.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A view from the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit as it drifts away with the ejected junk of the ''Avenger'']]
Solo had attached the ''Millennium Falcon'' to the backside of the ''Avenger''{{'s}} bridge command tower, where the Imperial Starfleet neglected to look. Solo knew that, per standard Imperial procedure, large warships such as the ''Avenger'' customarily jettisoned their garbage allotment before entering hyperspace. When the Imperial fleet, having conducted a scan of the area in the Anoat system,<ref name="ESB" /> finally decided that their prey had indeed escaped into hyperspace and began exiting the area themselves, Solo simply allowed his ship to tumble away undetected with the rest of the ''Avenger''{{'s}} refuse.<ref name="ESB novel" />

====Bounty hunter junk====
{{Quote|It was ingenious. It should have worked. If only Fett wasn't so ingenious as well.|Historian Voren Na'al, regarding Han Solo's evasion of the Empire&mdash;but not of Boba Fett&mdash;in the asteroid field|<ref name="GG3" />}}
Even before the Battle of Hoth began, the Empire had announced a reward for any bounty hunters who helped chase the Rebels fleeing from the system. Once it became clear to Vader that the ineptitude of his own fleet would likely never bring him those he sought, he sent out his own call for an elite group of hunters to capture the crew of the ''Millennium Falcon'' hiding within the asteroid field. Six bounty hunters, highlighted by the notorious [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], were instructed to rendezvous with Vader's ''Executor'' just outside the field, where they were briefed on the details of their mission.<ref name="Boba" />

[[File:BountyHunters.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Bounty hunters aboard the ''Executor''.]]
Just as Vader's briefing was finished, the ''Avenger''{{'s}} failure to capture the ''Millennium Falcon'' was reported throughout the fleet. The hunter [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]] surmised correctly&mdash;albeit too late&mdash;that Solo had hidden his ship within the asteroids, taking advantage of the fact that the high metal concentration of the field would distort sensor readings and help mask his location.<ref name="Payback" />

His own [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]]-long search within the field came to an abrupt end when one of his own strategically-placed [[Sensor beacon/Legends|sensor beacons]], powerful enough to counteract the metal-induced distortions, detected a badly damaged ''Millennium Falcon'' limping away from the system at [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] speed. Before Dengar could close in on his prey, however, a taunting transmission from the rival Fett activated a preemptively planted bomb within Dengar's ship, destroying the [[Engine/Legends|engines]] and neutralizing the craft. Dengar could only watch helplessly from the asteroids as Fett tracked Solo's departure away from the field.<ref name="Payback" />

===Legend of the exogorth===
{{Quote|It's interesting that while the ''Falcon'' was making history in the Galactic Civil War, it was also shedding some light on some old spacer folklore.|Historian Voren Na'al, regarding the Rebels' journey through the asteroid field|<ref name="GG3" />}}
The existence of an enormous space slug within the asteroid field had been written off as spacer legend until Solo's run-in with the creature,<ref name="OSVC 13" /> which the captain reported after rejoining the Alliance Fleet. Rebel [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] learned of the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} asteroid field ventures from Solo, and noted in his [[Voren Na'al's journal|journal]] details about the field and the incredible discovery of the giant space slug. Na'al further recorded that the findings shed light on the legends of Clabburn's space slugs in the asteroid belt.<ref name="GG3" />

Still, some continued to disbelieve the story given Solo's reputation for exaggeration.<ref name="OSVC 13" /> Reports of exogorth encounters such as Solo's alerted [[Biologist/Legends|biologists]] to their existence and offered a mystery as to how such enormous beasts came to thrive among the asteroids. To their shock, they eventually discovered that the exogorths engorged on asteroid rock, with the dual purpose of nutrition and burrowing.<ref name="FF67" />

===Darksaber Project===
====Mining failure====
{{Main|Darksaber (superweapon)}}
{{Quote|This is the most deadly part of the asteroid belt. None of our scout ships even dare to enter here.''"<br />"''Then the Rebels will be too frightened to follow us.|[[Sulamar]] and Durga the Hutt, who orders the Darksaber to be piloted on what would prove a fatal course|<ref name="Darksaber" />}}
[[File:DarksaberConstruction-TEC.jpg|thumb|right|280px|The Darksaber under construction]]
By 12 ABY,<ref name="Darksaber date" /> when the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] was largely governed by the Rebel Alliance's successor, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] criminal empire had created the [[Orko SkyMine Asteroid Processing Corporation]] under the direction of the Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|overlord]] [[Durga Besadii Tai]]<ref name="Darksaber" /> in what the corporation described as "the largest mining venture ever undertaken in the asteroid belt."<ref name="Illustrated" /> In reality, the corporation was nothing but a sham commercial enterprise designed to mask the copious amounts of funds being diverted into the Hutts' true goal: the construction of a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] powerful enough to rule the entire galaxy. Nicknamed the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|Darksaber Project]] by its chief [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]], [[Bevel Lemelisk]], the weapon would be constructed within the heart of the asteroid field itself, created from the asteroids' metal ore. The remote location of the Hoth system and the field's limitless resources made the Hoth asteroid belt the perfect construction site.<ref name="Darksaber" />

Early construction phases consisted of extracting the precious metal from the asteroids using two massive [[Automated Mineral Exploiter]]s, named [[Mineral Exploiter Alpha|Alpha]] and [[Mineral Exploiter Beta|Beta]], respectively. The processing units were little more than [[Cargo container/Legends|cargo containers]] equipped with [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] to reduce an asteroid to small debris before a forward mouth would swallow the rubble, spit out the useless slag, and retain the valuable ore. Each exploiter was designed to lock onto the heaviest concentration of metal in its general vicinity and commence with processing. The two machines each met their demise when they unexpectedly detected each other as sources of incredibly pure metal and ground one another down to scrap&mdash;a disappointing but ultimately minor setback for the Hutt operation.<ref name="Darksaber" />

A file on the Hoth asteroid belt's resources had been made by Orko SkyMine to prepare for the project, and the [[Unidentified author|author]], having witnessed the mining disaster from a former pirate base in the field along with their Orko SkyMine team, wrote an incident report on the failure of the Mineral Exploiters. Their identity was subsequently purged&mdash;and the being potentially destroyed&mdash;by a displeased Durga the Hutt.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Fearful of Durga's retribution for his faulty designs, Lemelisk declared the two Mineral Exploiters prototypes and promised to correct the programming error in the second batch: Exploiters [[Mineral Exploiter Delta|Delta]] and [[Mineral Exploiter Gamma|Gamma]].<ref name="Darksaber" />

====The saber takes shape====
The new mineral smelters, altered to ignore one another as a potential metal resource, proceeded with greater efficiency than their predecessors. Before long, the Darksaber weapon itself began to take shape among the asteroids: a long cylindrical shaft housing a planet-destroying [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] derived from the original [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. Seeing that his creation would resemble a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] hilt with extended blade when fired, Lemelisk derisively coined the project Darksaber, much to the amusement of Durga.<ref name="Darksaber" />

The Hutt had tasked the project's labor to multitudes of multi-armed, mind-linked creatures known as the [[Taurill/Legends|Taurill]], who were fitted with [[Environment suit/Legends|vacuum suits]] enabling them to manually build the weapon from the gravitation-void of space. Construction was delayed several times due to the easily distracted nature of the Taurill. Governed by an [[Taurill Overmind|Overmind]], in which each member of the hive was [[Hive mind/Legends|linked mentally]], the attention of the Taurill was occasionally diverted by a nearby passing asteroid or a smuggling ship that had entered the area. When the Taurill returned to their labor, they would continue construction on a different portion of the Darksaber superstructure, destroying previously created cohesiveness.<ref name="Darksaber" />

====Meeting the New Republic====
[[File:Darksaber.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Darksaber superweapon, under attack by New Republic forces in the asteroid field]]
Following the Jedi Luke Skywalker's unsuccessful journey to the planet Hoth to help the Jedi Knight [[Callista Ming]] regain control of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Skywalker and Ming entered the asteroid field in a barely functioning space [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]], damaged on the ice planet by [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]]. With [[Life support/Legends|life support]] systems failing on the ship, Skywalker [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathically]] communicated with Leia Organa Solo, his sister, across the vastness of space to call for help. Guided by the siblings' connection through the Force, she and Han Solo tracked down the damaged yacht and rescued the two stranded Jedi. However, they were unaware that the Hutt superweapon that the New Republic had recently become privy to was being constructed in the very same asteroid field.<ref name="Darksaber" />

The Darksaber project was discovered almost immediately thereafter by a search-and-destroy mission led by New Republic General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]]. Madine and two other [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] entered the field in [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptors]], although one of the pilots, [[Korenn]], was killed by a colliding asteroid, and infiltrated the construction site in self-propelled vac-suits. Despite the capture and death of both Madine and his fellow agent, [[Trandia]], a distress signal transmitted by Madine through the HoloNet directly to the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] prompted a response by a task force led by General [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]].<ref name="Darksaber" />

Antilles' fleet surged through the field, suffering considerable damage as they approached the Darksaber, which had fled into the most chaotic part of the belt on Durga's orders. [[Battle for the Darksaber|Pummeled]] by a salvo of [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire from the pursuing New Republic warships, the Hutt superweapon was ultimately obliterated between two massively sandwiching asteroids, killing Durga and creating yet more scattered debris among the field.<ref name="Darksaber" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|Sir, it's quite possible this asteroid is not entirely stable.''"<br />"''Not entirely stable? I'm glad you're here to tell us these things.|C-3PO makes an observation, to the annoyance of Han Solo|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:SWM14-RoguesAndVillainsCoverArt.png|thumb|right|330px|The ''Millennium Falcon'' maneuvering the myriad asteroids of the field.]]
In addition to various pirate bases, the Hoth asteroid field contained mining shafts<ref name="Illustrated" /> and stations.<ref name="Power" /> Clabburn the Elder's strongholds were built in the larger asteroids,<ref name="Illustrated" /> and similarly, Airtight Base, the pirate stronghold of Clabburn the Younger, was built inside a large asteroid.<ref name="Rough" /> Among the most massive asteroids in the field was the Big One,<ref name="Big One" /> which was home to an exogorth wherein the ''Millennium Falcon'' briefly hid during its escape from the Imperial fleet.<ref name="ESB" />

The legend of the asteroid Kerane's Folly told of it consisting almost entirely of platinum, but prospectors had repeatedly failed to rediscover the famed rock.<ref name="Illustrated" /> Yet another member of the field was the Poison Moon, named for its surface appearance, where the Jedi constrained a rogue member of their Order.<ref name="Poison" /> The Darksaber superweapon was constructed in the asteroid field and, as with many vessels that have ventured into it, was destroyed therein.<ref name="Darksaber" />

==Behind the scenes==
===First appearances and naming===
The Hoth asteroid field first appeared simultaneously in [[Donald F. Glut]]'s [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] and [[Shep Steneman]]'s ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'' adaptation of the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']];<ref name="ESB novel" /><ref name="ESB Storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> both were published on [[April 12]], [[1980]], just prior to the [[Irvin Kershner]] film's [[May]] theatrical release.<ref name="Amazon-RandomHouse">{{Amazon|url=Empire-Strikes-Back-Storybook/dp/0394844149|text=The Empire Strikes Back Storybook}}</ref><ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> [[West End Games]] sources provided two alternative names for the Hoth asteroid field: [[1993]]'s ''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]'', refers to it as the "Anoat Asteroid Belt,"<ref name="MTS" /> while the [[roleplaying game]] adventure "[[The Treasure of Celis Mott]]," published in [[1996]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''{{'s}} ''[[Instant Adventures]]'' book, names it the "Hoth Belt."<ref name="TCM">{{WEGCite|story=The Treasure of Celis Mott|book=Instant Adventures}}</ref> [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[2001]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]'' later gives the full name "Hoth Asteroid Belt."<ref name="Rebellion Era" />

===Production of ''The Empire Strikes Back''===
====Conception and development====
{{Music1|The Asteroid Field.flac|"The Asteroid Field," by John Williams|London Symphony Orchestra}}
[[File:MCQ-spaceslug.jpg|thumb|left|330px|Ralph McQuarrie's concept art for the space slug]]
The idea of entering an asteroid field to escape the enemy first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]]' [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of the original [[1977]] [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']] film, in which General Skywalker enters the [[Norton Asteroid Belt]] to elude Imperial forces. While the chase through the asteroid belt is included in every version of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' screenplay, some versions place the sequence after the ''Millennium Falcon'' reaches the Rebels' rendezvous point, where the ship is met by a massive Imperial fleet.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back''{{'s}} original script, Hoth and its system's asteroid belt are located in a region of space known as the [[Granita Clusta]]. The second draft of the script introduces the mynock attack on the Rebels inside the large asteroid.<ref name="Annotated">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref> Coupled with Darth Vader emerging from his [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber/Legends|meditation chamber]] and taking orders from the hitherto unseen Emperor at the same point in the film, the revelation that the "asteroid cave"&mdash;in which the Rebels were taking shelter and where Han Solo and Leia Organa opened themselves to love&mdash;was a space slug is drawn from the mythological motif of the [[Wikipedia:Hero's journey#Belly_of_the_Whale|journey into the belly of the beast]], symbolizing consumption and rebirth.<ref name="Myth">[[Star Wars: The Magic of Myth (book)|''Star Wars: The Magic of Myth'']]</ref>

The concert piece "[[The Asteroid Field]]," which was composed by [[John Williams]] as part of the [[London Symphony Orchestra]]&ndash;performed [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back Original Soundtrack|score]] to ''The Empire Strikes Back'', is dedicated to the chase of the ''Millennium Falcon'' through the Hoth asteroid field.<ref name="ESB soundtrack">[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back Original Soundtrack|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'' Original Soundtrack]]</ref> The brief moment of calm within the asteroid field benefitted from a sense of mystery, which was created by the use of [[Wikipedia:String instrument|string instruments]], a [[Wikipedia:Celesta|celeste]], a [[Wikipedia:Harp|harp]], and [[Wikipedia:Synthesizer|synthesizer]] in Williams' score during the mynock scene.<ref name="ESB SE soundtrack">''[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back Special Edition: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack]]''</ref>

====Industrial Light & Magic====
=====Solid foundations=====
[[File:FalconIntoCrater-MOTESB.png|thumb|right|360px|Hoth asteroid field concept art, by Ralph McQuarrie]]
Based on conceptual art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] and storyboards by [[Joe Johnston]], [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], and [[Dave Carson]],<ref name="Storyboards">''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref> designers at [[Industrial Light & Magic]] (ILM)&mdash;newly headquartered at the Kerner Building in [[Wikipedia:San Rafael, California|San Rafael]], [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]]<ref name="L&M" />&mdash;used between twenty-five to twenty-six different visual elements in one scene to create the chase through the Hoth asteroid field.<ref name="MOTESB doc">''[[The Making of "The Empire Strikes Back"]]''</ref> With some shots in the film containing thirty-eight elements, the asteroid field pursuit was its most complex [[Wikipedia:bluescreen|bluescreen]] sequence, encompassing shots of the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit interior, shots of various ''Falcon'' models, and shots of separate Star Destroyer models, TIE fighter models, and asteroid models,<ref name="SP FX">''[[SP FX: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> in addition to [[Wikipedia:Matte painting|matte paintings]] and sets for asteroid surfaces and starfields.<ref name="MOTESB">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

On [[December 8]], [[1978]], visual effects photography director [[Dennis Muren]] decided, with others' input, that asteroid explosions would be shot live on film before being re-photographed in [[Wikipedia:Rotoscoping|rotoscope]], where the [[Wikipedia:Matte (filmmaking)|mattes]] could be composited for complex actions. Photography at ILM began in [[February]] [[1979]], with work being done on the asteroid sequence, among others, although the crew were limited to the use of only two cameras&mdash;the [[John Dykstra]]&ndash;developed Dykstraflex and another motion control [[Wikipedia:Technirama|Technirama]]&mdash;until August. Before principle photography commenced under Director of Photography [[Peter Suschitzky]] in [[Wikipedia:England|England's]] [[Elstree Studios]] later in spring, Muren, to ensure consistency in lighting, asked him to shine the key lights from the left when the Rebels approach the asteroids.<ref name="MOTESB" />

=====Asteroids, asteroids, and more asteroids=====
{{Quote|Not only is it funny, but it keeps you thinking about what's the best, fastest, cheapest way to do this. You know, it's every producer's dream.|Visual Effects Supervisor Ken Ralston, regarding the use of potatoes as asteroids|<ref name="L&M">{{LightAndMagic|Just Think About It}}</ref>}}
[[File:Asteroid_box.jpg|thumb|left|330px|The "asteroid box"]]
Among the visual elements were hundreds of asteroids, including those in an<ref name="Livestream">{{SWYouTube|video=cfqopSob_IU|text=ILM Presents: "Empire at 40"|date=2020-05-28}}</ref> "asteroid box,"<ref name="Databank" /> "asteroid big box,"<ref name="MOTESB doc" /> or "asteroid mover,"<ref name="Livestream" /> that had various layers<ref name="MOTESB doc" /> and was composed of thirty to forty small clay rocks suspended from black rotating<ref name="Livestream" /> monofilament strings,<ref name="MOTESB" /> which were connected from above by a chain operated by a crank, to represent an extensive asteroid cluster.<ref name="Livestream" /> The motorized machine, which had hundreds of gears and rotated asteroids at varying speeds with repeatable moves, was engineered by Supervising Stage Technician [[Ted Moehnke]].<ref name="ASC box">{{WebCite|url=https://theasc.com/magazine/starwars/gallery/empire/ilm/img3.htm|text=O Pioneers! or Inside ILM &#45; The Empire Strikes Back - Image 3|work=[https://theasc.com The American Society of Cinematographers]|archivedate=20230105122121}}</ref>

Asteroids closer to the viewer were represented by pieces of polystyrene coated in plaster,<ref name="Databank" /> attached to pronged pipes, and painted at the ILM model shop by artists such as [[Steve Gawley]].<ref name="L&M" /> Gawley and other modellists initially had to spend some time on determining the best way to create the look of the asteroids.<ref name="Dreams">''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> Visual effects cameraman [[Ken Ralston]], due to the tediousness in making the models and him thinking that they looked like [[Wikipedia:Potato|potatoes]], at one point purchased with his assistant, [[Selwyn Eddy]], some actual potatoes in place of the polystyrene asteroids.<ref name="L&M" /> The potatoes were smoother than the asteroid pieces and flew by the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit in the final cut.<ref name="MOTESB" /> A tennis shoe was also included among the asteroids.<ref name="Livestream" />

[[File:Thejawsthatbite.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Lorne Peterson with his space slug jaw model]]
For the large asteroid the Rebels fly into, both a combination model of at least the crater and the surrounding surface as well as matte paintings were used<ref name="Databank" /> against a black backing.<ref name="Nicholson">{{WebCite|url=https://theasc.com/magazine/starwars/articles/empire/comop|text=Composite Optical Photography for The Empire Strikes Back|author=Nicholson, Bruce|work=[https://theasc.com The American Society of Cinematographers]|archivedate=20230105131655}}</ref> The crater set, measuring around thirty feet in diameter, was built by Joe Johnston, [[Michael Pangrazio]], and [[Chris Anderson (artist)|Chris Anderson]]<ref name="MOTESB" /> out of dense foam and topped with white dust<ref name="Asteroid surface prop">{{WebCite|url=https://propstore.com/product/star-wars-the-empire-strikes-back-1980/asteroid-surface-model-miniature|text=Asteroid Surface Model Miniature|work=[https://propstore.com Propstore]|archivedate=20230106213613}}</ref> on [[May 4]], with Pangrazio also having done the matte paintings of larger asteroids and starfields using oil paints. The model shop's rubber hand puppet for the space slug would be added to the crater set, and on [[September 4]] ILM decided to wait until the slug is completed before determining the look of the asteroid/space slug tunnel that the ''Falcon'' would fly though.<ref name="MOTESB" /> For a closer shot of the space slug's jaws, a large model was made by the model shop's supervisor, [[Lorne Peterson]].<ref name="Sculpting">''[[Sculpting a Galaxy: Inside the Star Wars Model Shop]]''</ref>

On [[May 11]], associate producer [[Jim Bloom]] split shooting at ILM three-ways between Muren, Ken Ralston on nightshift, and effects cameraman [[Jim Veilleux]] filming asteroid belt and starfield paintings.<ref name="MOTESB" /> The film's final cut includes one of the gag footages shot by Ralston, where the camera skims over an asteroid surface. The latter part of the footage was cut: the camera goes on to approach a mock&ndash;space slug puppet, made from an old sock, that exits a crater and attacks one of the two TIE fighters flying overhead.<ref name="DefCol">''[[Star Wars Trilogy: The Definitive Collection]]'' commentary</ref>

=====Boulder innovations=====
{{Quote|It became clear that the myriad elements sent to optical for compositing were much more complex and dynamic than had ever been done on film before. To see completed shots of the ''Falcon'' in the asteroid field or snowspeeders against beautiful aerial plates shot in Norway was truly amazing.|Matte painter [[Harrison Ellenshaw]]|<ref name="MOTESB" />}}
All of these elements were shot separately against a bluescreen using motion-control photography<ref name="Edlund">{{WebCite|url=https://theasc.com/articles/flashback-star-wars-episode-v-the-empire-strikes-back|text=Special Visual Effects for Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back|author=Edlund, Richard|work=[https://theasc.com The American Society of Cinematographers]|archivedate=20230105122422}}</ref> before being composited with "the Quad"&mdash;an [[Wikipedia:Optical printer|optical printer]] that ILM, whose optical photography department for ''Empire'' was headed by [[Bruce Nicholson]], built themselves.<ref name="MOTESB doc" /> The approach was pioneered by visual effects co-supervisor [[Richard Edlund]], complete with unprecedented computer-controlled capabilities<ref name="Nicholson" /> and other technological workarounds. The machine was not operational until late [[October]] 1979. Some shots of the ''Falcon'' and TIEs in the asteroid field had to go through the Quad four times to ensure the color timing was correct and the matte lines were eliminated.<ref name="MOTESB" />

Filming of the elements that would be fed into the optical printer had taken place<ref name="MOTESB doc" /> over many months, with asteroid sequence tests taking place from late March, 1979, and the first test asteroid shot being composited on [[April 6]]. It was deemed to be discombobulated and distracting from dramatic impact and had to be simplified.<ref name="MOTESB" /> The asteroids initially coming every which way produced a disorientating effect; in order to create a sense of direction and threat from the asteroids, Johnston and Muren had redesigned the asteroid sequence's shots so that the rocks came largely from one direction. Ralston additionally programmed the movement of the ships and asteroids in the asteroid field sequences to create a vivid and kinetic sense of dynamism,<ref name="Livestream" /> and animatics of the chase created by ILM's animation department allowed editors to more easily coordinate the timing and pacing of the scene.<ref name="AOSWEVTESB">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Shots of the ''Falcon'' weaving through asteroids laterally were filmed in early [[June]],<ref name="MOTESB doc" /> and most of the effects shots for the asteroid sequence were in place by the time of the first cut's completion by [[October 17]].<ref name="MOTESB" />

Lucas' [[Wikipedia:Sergei Eisenstein|Eisensteinian]] film editing philosophies in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' came into play as he had to consider the screen directions of objects flying past the camera while cutting the film over and over again. On [[October 31]], Joe Johnston and his assistants used Lucas' cutting copy to sketch the frame composition and continuity of effect sequences. From those sketches came storyboards, which informed camera crew and model builders the angles and moves their miniatures had to make.<ref name="MOTESB" /> On [[November 7]], George Lucas and ILM screened clips of the sequence to discuss further adjustments.<ref name="Journal">''[[Once Upon a Galaxy: A Journal of the Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Notably, the editing and shot composition of the asteroid sequence contains some esoteric moments, such as the ''Falcon'' leaving the frame prior to entering the big asteroid.<ref name="MOTESB" />

====Asteroids? What asteroids?====
{{Quote|The worst is when we're in the cockpit and you're supposed to see stars or asteroids or whatever special effect, but we don't see anything. We're looking at a corner of a camera and screaming, 'WHAT ARE YOU GOING INTO AN ASTEROID FIELD FOR?!' Or, 'THERE'S SOMETHING OUT THERE!'<nowiki />|Carrie Fisher, about filming in the cockpit|<ref name="MOTESB" />}}
When filming on Elstree Studios' Stage 5 in [[March]] 1979, Darth Vader actor [[David Prowse]] would alter his lines for a laugh, with "The asteroids do not concern me, I want that ship" being spoken as "[[Wikipedia:Hemorrhoid|Hemorrhoids]] do not concern me, I need a shit." Producer [[Gary Kurtz]] observed that the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit set, with blue screens placed around it on Stage 8 of Elstree Studios in the summer, was the most challenging, especially for the actors. [[Carrie Fisher]], the actress playing Princess Leia Organa, found the blue screens hard to work with as she would have to scream at imaginery asteroids; [[Harrison Ford]] once took up a [[Wikipedia:Saw|saw]] in anger and sawed through the set. Even Peter Suschitzky required some help with lighting the set, and Irvin Kershner had some difficultly handling the special effects, blue screen, and matte painting scenes.<ref name="MOTESB" />

For the "asteroid cave"&mdash;more accurately the space slug interior&mdash;filming took place on [[June 18]] on Elstree's Stage 6,<ref name="MOTESB" /> which featured the ''Millennium Falcon'' exterior and was laid with black [[Wikipedia:Visqueen|Visqueen]] plastic sheets and dry ice clouding the stage floor, surrounded by draping black curtains.<ref name="365 Days">''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]''</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
Several ''Star Wars'' sources depict C-3PO as providing Han Solo with different odds for navigating an asteroid field: the novelization of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' and the film's [[Star Wars (1977)|''Marvel Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] adaptation, [[Star Wars (1977) 41|''Star Wars'' (1977) 41]] include odds of 2,467 to 1;<ref name="ESB novel" /><ref name="Marvel">[[Star Wars (1977) 41|''Star Wars'' (1977) 41]]</ref> the plot synopsis of [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back - Official Collectors Edition|''The Empire Strikes Back - Official Collectors Edition'' magazine]] places the odds at 365,000 to one;<ref name="ESB Official Collectors Edition">''[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back - Official Collectors Edition]]''</ref> the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' lists odds of 725 to 1;<ref name="ESB radio">[[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]]</ref> while the radio drama's script, originally published in ''[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization]]'', puts the odds at 720 to 1.<ref name="ESB script">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>

[[Dave Wolverton]]'s short story "[[Payback: The Tale of Dengar]]," which was published in 1996's ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'' anthology and details Dengar's search of Han Solo and the ''Millennium Falcon'' through the asteroid field, describes nearly a half-hour passing between the time the Imperial fleet enters hyperspace and the ''Millennium Falcon'', having hidden itself in the Star Destroyer ''Avenger''{{'s}} jettisoned garbage dump, begins to limp out of the system, while Dengar is ultimately left incapacitated within the asteroid field. This time is seemingly inconsistent with the film ''The Empire Strikes Back'', which depicts the ''Millennium Falcon'' as beginning its departure from the region immediately after the departure of the Imperial fleet.<ref name="Payback" />

[[Kevin J. Anderson]]'s [[1995]] reference title ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' specifies that the Hoth asteroid field was formed from a collision "billions of years" before the Galactic Civil War,<ref name="Illustrated" /> whereas Wizards of the Coast's 2001 roleplaying guide ''Rebellion Era Sourcebook'' mentions that it occurred "millions of years" ago instead.<ref name="Rebellion Era" /> This article treats the original information of billions of years as correct.

===Video games===
The [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' ([[2006]]) and ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' ([[2007]]), which are [[Canon|non-canonical]] to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, recreate the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} flight through the asteroid field, adding unique game mechanics not seen in the film.<ref name="LEGO OT">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref><ref name="LEGO">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> [[Wikipedia:Nintendo GameCube|Nintendo GameCube's]] ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'', released in [[2001]], offers the Hoth asteroid field as a bonus level that closely resembles the film's storyline, in which the player must also recreate the ''Falcon''{{'s}} chase through the field before completing the level by attaching the ship to the backside of a Star Destroyer's bridge tower.<ref name="RSII">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref> In [[2003]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Flight of the Falcon]]'' for [[Wikipedia:Game Boy Advance|Game Boy Advance]], the player enters hyperspace at the conclusion of the game's asteroid field level, a clear contradiction of established canon in ''Star Wars'' Legends.<ref name="Flight">''[[Star Wars: Flight of the Falcon]]''</ref>

===Cultural impact===
The asteroid field and protagonists featured in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' has inspired the naming of two cameras&mdash;LUKE (LICIACube Unit Key Explorer) and LEIA (LICIACube Explorer Imaging for Asteroid)&mdash;installed on the [[Wikipedia:LICIACube|LICIACube]] satellite, part of [[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA's]] [[Wikipedia:Double Asteroid Redirection Test|Double Asteroid Redirection Test]] mission in [[2022]] to test ways of [[Wikipedia:Asteroid impact avoidance|preventing asteroid impacts]] on [[Wikipedia:Earth|Earth]].<ref name="DART">{{WebCite|url=https://cosmosmagazine.com/space/watch-the-dart-asteroid-impact|text=DART Spacecraft impacts asteroid Dimorphos, LICIACube to sweep crash site|author=Agius, Matthew|date=27-09-2022|work=[https://cosmosmagazine.com Cosmos]|archivedate=20230101002121}}</ref>
